text.text: The SMT surface-mount soldering process is employed to solder the MCU, MOSFETs, and other components onto the circuit board. After powering on, the voltage output and PWM signal feedback are checked to ensure they are functioning correctly.
The brushless motor is embedded within a dedicated bracket; the motor's three-phase wires are securely soldered to the PCB, and insulated using heat-shrink tubing.
PTC Heating Element Installation: Secure the PTC element onto a mica support, with mica insulation layers covering both sides.
Align the impeller with the motor shaft and press until it snaps into the groove; then install the air guide shroud, ensuring that there are no burrs inside the air duct.
Front Housing Assembly: Embedded filter; Rear Housing Assembly: Power cord and mode switch installed.
The upper and lower housings are aligned and joined using ultrasonic welding and high-temperature-resistant latches, followed by an airtightness test.
Cold Air Mode: Runs at full speed for 5 minutes. Hot Air Mode: Runs continuously for 40 minutes and monitors the temperature gradient.
The product is packaged in sturdy cardboard boxes to ensure safe handling and transport.
To ensure the product receives additional protection during long-distance transport, please place it in a flight case.

Our standard lead time is approximately 30–35 business days after receipt of the deposit; however, depending on raw material availability, the shipping cycle for certain models and colors may be as short as 25 days or less.
Which mode of transportation do you use?
Via sea or air freight. We have contracts with numerous freight forwarders and express service providers.

What is the difference between a traditional hair dryer and a high-speed hair dryer?

The primary differences between traditional hair dryers and high-speed hair dryers lie in their motors, airflow speed, temperature, and additional features. High-speed hair dryers typically utilize brushless motors, offering faster rotational speeds and higher airflow velocities; moreover, they often incorporate hair-care functions—such as negative ion technology—to protect the hair. In contrast, traditional hair dryers predominantly employ carbon-brush motors, which generate lower airflow speed
